title: Cross-border traffic-fine enforcement — Czech bill transposing Directive (EU) 2024/3237 hands municipal offices translated notices, driver tracing and EU-wide fine collection
money_note: No money is attached to the need. The explanatory memorandum costs only the transport ministry's one-off IT extension of the EUCARIS link at 3,000,000 CZK, absorbed in existing budgets, and says municipalities need no investment; nothing is scored or converted.
summary: A transport-ministry bill in inter-ministerial comment would transpose Directive (EU) 2024/3237 from 20 July 2027, widening the list of road offences that trigger cross-border data exchange, translated information forms and cross-border collection of fines. Municipal offices with extended powers carry the new casework, and every vehicle operator must name the driver for offences committed elsewhere in the EU.
notes: STATUS: DRAFT — government bill amending Act 361/2000 Sb. (road traffic) and related acts, VeKLEP material KORNDY2GNBC7, stage '2 - v připomínkovém řízení', first published 21 Sep 2026; nothing in it is in force. Read from the Důvodová zpráva (attachment KORNDY5NPDVJ, saved pages/veklep/zd_KORNDY2GNBC7.docx/.txt), the předkládací zpráva (zp_KORNDY2GNBC7) and the bill text (ma_KORNDY2GNBC7). DATES: Čl. VI — the act takes effect 1 Jul 2027, but the cross-border provisions take effect 20 Jul 2027 (the Directive's transposition deadline) and the B-licence 4,250 kg alternative-fuel equivalence from Directive (EU) 2025/2205 on 26 Nov 2027. No RIA was prepared (the 2026 legislative plan waived it). WHAT THE DZ STATES: 12,144 information forms were sent in 2024 and 2025 under the road-traffic act; about 96 % of municipal cross-border queries concern speeding; the largest increase is expected from overweight offences caught by high-speed weigh-in-motion, 'řádově ... ročně stovky'; the changes 'budou mít významné dopady na obecní úřady obcí s rozšířenou působností a částečně také na krajské úřady' (tracing drivers, translating the extended form and parts of decisions, serving other states' documents, passing fines for cross-border collection); public-notice service is excluded for these offences; the ministry pays for translating the generic form text and expects offices to translate case parts with machine tools such as the Commission's eTranslation; collection of foreign fines moves to the Customs Administration under the tax code; the ministry becomes national contact point. WHO MUST ACT: ORP municipal offices and regional offices (appeals), the Police and the road-transport inspectorate (annual statistics to the ministry), vehicle operators including fleet, rental and leasing firms (driver identification for offences abroad). Also in the bill: driving-licence validity 10 -> 15 years for AM-B+E, traffic-psychologist accreditation and fines up to 500,000 CZK, psychological testing for drivers of emergency vehicles with a two-year transition. DEDUP: corpus searched for 2024/3237, 2015/413, přeshraniční, cross-border fine/offence, KORNDY2GNBC7 — only the unrelated road-traffic card veklep-KORNDK9DFTG2 (ITS data); the card veklep-KORNDY2GNBC7 is being surfaced by this run's scripted veklep fetch.
quote: V letech 2024 a 2025 bylo odesláno 12 144 informačních formulářů podle zákona o silničním provozu.

title: Air passenger rights reform — Regulation (EU) 2026/2202 rewrites EU261 compensation, information and complaint-handling duties for airlines, ticket sellers and airports from 23 October 2027
money_note: No money is attached to the need. The regulation sets per-passenger compensation amounts (EUR 250 / 400 / 600) but no budget or market figure; nothing is scored.
summary: Regulation (EU) 2026/2202, published on 2 October 2026 and applying from 23 October 2027, replaces the EU261 compensation article, obliges airlines to tell entitled passengers within 96 hours how to claim, and requires every air carrier and intermediary to run a complaint-handling mechanism with fixed reply deadlines. It also adds information duties for sellers of separate air contracts and a mandatory rights notice at airport check-in and gates.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — Regulation (EU) 2026/2202 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 September 2026 amending Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 and Council Regulation (EC) No 2027/97, OJ L 2 Oct 2026, adopted on the Conciliation Committee joint text of 15 Jun 2026; read in full from CELLAR (CELEX 32026R2202, saved pages/eu/32026R2202.raw and 32026R2202-en.txt). DATES: in force on the 20th day after publication; 'It shall apply from 23 October 2027.' WHO MUST ACT: operating air carriers (new Art. 7: EUR 250 for journeys up to 1,500 km, EUR 400 for intra-Union journeys above 1,500 km and other journeys of 1,500-3,500 km, EUR 600 otherwise, with a 50 % reduction on long-haul if arrival is no more than four hours late; compensation when arriving more than three hours late; reimbursement offer when departure delay reaches five hours; disembarkation after a two-hour tarmac delay; information on the right to compensation and how to claim within 96 hours, on a durable medium; payment by electronic bank transfer unless otherwise agreed; burden of proof on the carrier); air carriers AND intermediaries (Art. 15a complaint mechanism: acknowledge within seven working days, reasoned reply within one month or a final reply within two months; no user account or app may be required to receive documents or boarding passes; separate-contract warnings before purchase); airport managing bodies (rights notice displayed at check-in, self-service kiosks and gates). CZ angle: binds Czech carriers, online and high-street travel sellers acting as intermediaries, and Czech airports; claim-handling firms face a changed compensation schedule. DEDUP: corpus searched for 261/2004, air passenger, passenger rights, práva cestujících — only yc-airhelp (a claims company, 2013); no regulation record of the reform.
quote: the operating air carrier shall, within 96 hours of the termination of the journey, electronically provide the passenger, on a durable medium, with information on the passenger’s right to compensation, and clear instructions on how to submit a request for compensation.

title: Critical-infrastructure portal decree — interior-ministry decree 178/2026 Sb. makes the state portal the channel for CI entities' cooperation, incident reports and named-user registration from 1 October 2026
money_note: No money is attached to the need. The decree text states no cost; the 6M CZK interior-ministry portal figure recorded by the 2026-09-28 sweep comes from the draft's explanatory memorandum and is the state's own build cost, not money attached to the entities' duty; nothing is scored.
summary: Decree 178/2026 Sb., in force since 1 October 2026 under the critical-infrastructure act 266/2025 Sb., sets how essential-service providers and critical-infrastructure entities log into the state portal, register their authorised persons and critical suppliers, and file incident reports and other information in structured form. Each entity must keep its user list and data current under a minimisation rule.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — vyhláška č. 178/2026 Sb. ze dne 23. září 2026, o portálu kritické infrastruktury (Ministry of the Interior, issued under § 29(2) and implementing § 20(9) of Act 266/2025 Sb.); promulgated 30 Sep 2026, in force 1 Oct 2026 ('dnem následujícím po dni jejího vyhlášení'); read in full from the e-Sbírka sbr-cache fragment API (saved pages/esbirka/sb-2026-178.txt and sbr-2026-178.json). WHAT IT REQUIRES: access via the crisis-management information system with authenticated users (§ 2(1)); the portal is the route for cooperation with the administrator and for incident reports under §§ 18-19 of the CI act (§ 2(4)); each entity enters name or IČO, seat, contact e-mail and EU establishments, plus data on its critical suppliers and its CI manager (§ 3(1)); it notifies every authorised person with name, date of birth, role, phone and e-mail, access is individual and non-transferable, and the entity must keep the circle of users current (§ 4(2)-(4)); information goes in structured form via the UI, documents as PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PNG or JPG (§ 4(5)-(6)); the entity answers for accuracy and currency (§ 4(7)). DEDUP: the draft is held only as the metadata card veklep-KORNDTUBDJRM (2026-05-07); the parent act is reg-cer-zakon-266. This is the enacted instrument with its in-force date. Searched the corpus for: portál kritické infrastruktury, 178/2026, KORNDTUBDJRM.
quote: (4) Oprávněnému uživateli se prostřednictvím portálu umožňuje a) poskytovat součinnost správci a dalším oprávněným uživatelům v rozsahu nezbytném pro plnění povinností podle zákona o kritické infrastruktuře a b) hlásit incident podle § 18 a 19 zákona o kritické infrastruktuře.

title: Mid-year travel-allowance fuel price — labour-ministry decree 175/2026 Sb. raises the statutory average petrol price for employee car-use reimbursement from 34.70 to 41.80 CZK per litre from 1 October 2026
money_note: No money is attached to the need. The decree changes a per-litre reimbursement parameter; no aggregate cost is published in the decree, and nothing is estimated.
summary: Decree 175/2026 Sb. raises the average price of 95-octane petrol used to reimburse employees who drive their own cars on business from 34.70 CZK to 41.80 CZK per litre with effect from 1 October 2026. Every employer and payroll or expense system that reimburses business car use at the statutory average price must switch rates mid-year.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — vyhláška č. 175/2026 Sb. ze dne 25. září 2026, kterou se mění vyhláška č. 573/2025 Sb. (2026 travel-allowance rates, as amended by 78/2026 Sb.); issued by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs under § 189(2) of the labour code; promulgated 29 Sep 2026, in force 1 Oct 2026; read in full from the e-Sbírka sbr-cache fragment API (saved pages/esbirka/sb-2026-175.txt). WHAT IT CHANGES: § 4(a) of 573/2025 Sb., the average price of 95-octane petrol for reimbursing fuel when the employee does not document the actual price, 34.70 CZK -> 41.80 CZK. WHY: the draft's memorandum (VeKLEP KORNDXWQDTHG, read 2026-09-28) records the August 2026 average petrol price at 41.80 CZK/l, +20.46 % over the decree value, the labour-code trigger for an extraordinary revision; it follows the September 2026 supply shocks recorded in reg-pohonne-hmoty-strop-2026-10 (fuel price cap 172/2026 Sb.). It is the second amendment of the 2026 decree (78/2026 Sb. was the first). WHO MUST ACT: every employer reimbursing business use of employees' private cars under the labour code's travel-allowance rules, and public-sector employers paying travel allowances; rates apply to trips from 1 Oct 2026. DEDUP: corpus holds the draft cards veklep-KORNDXWQDTHG and veklep-KORNDTSAMQVA (an earlier 2026 rates card) only as metadata, and the fuel-cap record cites the trigger; this is the enacted instrument with its date and figure. Searched: 573/2025, cestovních náhrad, travel allowance.
quote: V § 4 písm. a) se částka „34,70 Kč“ nahrazuje částkou „41,80 Kč“.

title: CZ-DRG version 2027 — statistics office notice 174/2026 Sb. puts every acute-care hospital on new grouper software, coding rules and relative weights from 1 January 2027
money_note: No money is attached to the need. The notice publishes a classification and software versions, not a budget; the related draft update of the health-procedure list (VeKLEP KORNDVL9Q4OE) estimates 627-644M CZK of extra 2027 insurance spending, but that is a different instrument and a payer cost, so nothing is scored here.
summary: Czech Statistical Office notice 174/2026 Sb. announces CZ-DRG version 2027, effective 1 January 2027, with a new Pre-grouper and Grouper software release, a new definition manual, coding and reporting rules for diagnoses and a new table of relative weights. Every hospital providing acute in-patient care must code and report 2027 admissions under the new version, as it has had to after each earlier update of the classification.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — sdělení Českého statistického úřadu č. 174/2026 Sb. ze dne 24. září 2026, o aktualizaci Klasifikace hospitalizovaných pacientů (CZ-DRG); promulgated 29 Sep 2026; effective for 2027 from 1 Jan 2027; read in full from the e-Sbírka sbr-cache fragment API (saved pages/esbirka/sb-2026-174.txt). WHAT IT ISSUES for version 2027: (1) the case-building methodology with CZ-DRG Pre-grouper 2027 and its data interface, installation and technical documentation; (2) the classification definition manual with CZ-DRG Grouper 2027, DRG-marker methodology and the critical-procedure and marker code list; (3) diagnosis coding and reporting rules; (4) the relative-weight methodology, relevant-cost rules, case-costing methodology and the relative-weight code list. The Ministry of Health distributes the materials, ÚZIS is the service organisation, and the binding materials are on the ministry's CZ-DRG page and the DRG Restart portal. RECURRENCE: it amends notice 159/2018 Sb. for the eleventh time (253/2019, 67/2020, 385/2020, 217/2021, 385/2021, 80/2022, 302/2022, 300/2023, 281/2024, 363/2025). SAME DEADLINE, OTHER INSTRUMENT (context only, not this record): the draft amendment of the procedure-point list 134/1998 Sb. (VeKLEP KORNDVL9Q4OE, stage 6PK since 2 Oct 2026) adds 112 procedures, removes 19 and updates 256 for 2027. WHO MUST ACT: hospitals with acute in-patient care, their coding staff and hospital-information-system vendors, and the health-insurance funds that pay by DRG. DEDUP: corpus searched for CZ-DRG, DRG, 159/2018, 174/2026 — only the 2026 reimbursement decree reg-mzd-uhradova-432-2025, which uses DRG-based payment but is a different instrument.
